newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU may appeal against WTO banana ruling.
newsitem.headline: EU may appeal against WTO banana ruling.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it may appeal against a negative World Trade Organisation (WTO) ruling on the European Union's banana regime.
A WTO dispute panel on Tuesday confirmed a preliminary finding in March that the EU's banana import rules favoured imports from mainly Caribbean countries and violated open trading rules.
"Under WTO rules there is a right of appeal against the panel's conclusions," European Commission President Jacques Santer said in a statement.
Santer said the way in which the panel's confidential report interpreted essential WTO measures raised questions which went far beyond EU banana import rules.
He said the aim of the banana regime was to encourage the economic and social development of poor African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries which were highly dependent on banana exports.
"The Commission considers it extremely important that the interests of these regions and countries are not harmed," Santer said.
Earlier on Wednesday, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler had hinted at an appeal.
"...There is a question of an objection being raised," Fischler told a news conference. "(The ruling) is very technical, very dense, it will have to be examined very carefully indeed."
The confidential report will be distributed to other WTO members in three week's time after which the EU has had 60 days in which to raise objections.

The WTO panel was created in May 1996 following a complaint from the United States, Ecuador, Honduras, Mexico and Guatemala that EU banana import rules discriminated in favour of middlemen marketing EU and ACP bananas.
